clue.text: Preposterous seamen tried for East Enders' audition

indicators.note: the letters are what a Cockney listener would hear, the East End dropping its aitches

parts.note: ABS are able seamen, and a case that is tried is heard, which the East End says as 'EARD

explanation.surface: A Cockney hearing of some sailors' trial is ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: East Enders (Cockneys, from east London) drop the H, so ABS 'EARD (able seamen heard) is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives for something wildly unreasonable or ridiculous.

clue.text: Alarm when engineers put in anything worn

indicators.note: the engineers are placed inside the word for alarm

parts.note: to appal is to alarm, horrify
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Alarm spreads when engineers are put into protective gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing in general, whatever garments are worn on the body.

clue.text: Take tea, perhaps, without your sweetener

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, the drinking word surrounds the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink, taking tea being one example
YR is a short form of your in letters and texts

explanation.surface: Have your tea, but skip the sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick sugary liquid used to add sweetness to food and drink.

clue.text: Give more time to sextet in free concert?

indicators.note: the number sits inside the rearranged letters
set free, the letters of concert are rearranged

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A group of six playing a free concert, wondering if they will get extra stage time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give more time' means a fresh prison sentence, not more playing time; 'free' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To sentence again after a fresh guilty verdict, handing a criminal more time in jail.

clue.text: Commended installation of lift in Palladium

indicators.note: the lift is being installed, fitted within the element's symbol
together with installation of, places the lift within the chemical symbol

parts.note: Pd is the chemical symbol for palladium
to lift is to raise

explanation.surface: A lift has been fitted in the London Palladium theatre, and earned praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past forms of a verb meaning to speak well of, approve publicly.

clue.text: Coin once found in north-east France pocketed by doctor from south

indicators.note: in a down answer, read from the south means going upwards, so the letters are reversed
the doctor holds the other pieces in a pocket

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner
taken as written
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: An old coin turns up in north-east France, picked up by a doctor from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketed by' gives GINNEFP, and 'from south' reads it upwards, as a down answer is read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A small German unit of currency, a hundredth of a mark, before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Nutmeg, for one, having bottom pinched by a setter at lunch?

indicators.note: the a goes next to the shortened spice
in a down answer the bottom is the last letter, pinched means stolen

parts.note: nutmeg is a spice, and also this puzzle's setter

explanation.surface: The setter Nutmeg gets their bottom pinched by another setter over lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Nutmeg is this crossword's setter, so the surface is a cheeky joke at their own expense.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury jelly made from stock that sets around cold food, hence a setter at a meal.

clue.text: Master receiving kiss when artist finds flower

indicators.note: the master takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: a sage is a wise master
X is a written kiss
if can mean when, as in 'if it rains, we stay'
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A master painter gets a kiss when an artist finds a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockery plant with small star-shaped blooms, a genus of flowering plants.

clue.text: Three cardinals with boring clothing? Far from it

definitions.text: Three cardinals with boring clothing? Far from it

indicators.note: the dull word wraps round the points like a garment

parts.note: dry means dull, boring
E, S and S are three cardinal compass points

explanation.surface: Three cardinals dressed in boring robes? Not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' suggests churchmen in red but means compass points; the whole clue describes smart clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant or elaborate in style, the opposite of drab attire.

clue.text: Like posh children occupying seats, every other one being taken

indicators.note: the posh children sit within the remaining letters
alternate letters of seats are taken away, leaving the first, third and fifth

parts.note: U is upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Posh kids grab seats, taking every other one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every other one being taken' leaves S, A and S from seats, and 'occupying' puts U and CH within.
explanation.definitionFit: Both introduce examples: 'fruits like apples' equals 'fruits for example apples'.

clue.text: We may hear soldier bring down retardant from plane

indicators.note: says the letters come from how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: a soldier is a PARA (paratrooper), and to bring down a bird is to shoot it

explanation.surface: A soldier is overheard being told to shoot something down.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy that slows (retards) a fall from an aircraft; retardant here means a thing that slows descent.

clue.text: Very good team ultimately invincible, being out of this world

parts.note: PI is crossword shorthand for pious, very good
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of invincible

explanation.surface: An unbeaten team is out of this world, a sporting boast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of this world' looks like praise for the team, but with 'being' it defines a fairy creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mischievous fairy is a supernatural being, not of the ordinary world.

clue.text: Mature writer on Christian discipline?

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: RI is Religious Instruction, a school subject on Christianity
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author writes about Christian discipline, perhaps a mature thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: RI (Religious Instruction) is the old British name for RE lessons in schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To mature is to develop fully, as fruit does when it becomes ready to eat.

clue.text: 4 inch boxes for bracelets

parts.note: a hand is a measure of four inches, used for the height of horses
to box someone's ears is to cuff them

explanation.surface: Boxes four inches long to hold bracelets, a jeweller's packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a cross-reference to 4 across, but it is just the number four.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracelets is old slang for the metal restraints police put on a prisoner's wrists.

clue.text: Problems unloading weight on large trucks

indicators.note: the weight is taken off and the large one put on in its place

parts.note: worries are problems
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Heavy goods vehicles have trouble when unloading weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Both name large goods vehicles; the first is the usual British word, the second American.

clue.text: Irreverent drunk docking tail of deacon's dog

indicators.note: the drunken letters reel into a new order
docking a tail cuts it off, so the letter is removed
the last letter of deacon

explanation.surface: A drunken irreverent man cuts the tail of the deacon's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docking' removes N (tail of deacon) from IRREVERENT, and 'drunk' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of gun dog trained to fetch shot game, such as the golden or Labrador.

clue.text: Noted midday excursionist returns, confounded

indicators.note: the excursionist comes back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Noel Coward's song says 'Mad dogs and Englishmen go out in the midday sun'

explanation.surface: A famous lunchtime walker comes home baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: The song 'Mad Dogs and Englishmen' supplies the creature famous for midday outings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild oaths used as adjectives, like 'damned', expressing irritation.

clue.text: Afflicted in Paris — cold, shivering

indicators.note: shivering shakes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller in Paris is unwell, cold and shivering.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffering from dropsy, an old name for oedema, so afflicted by swelling.

clue.text: Retreating pets must keep it motionless

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole construction is read in reverse
the pets hold the word it inside them

parts.note: cats are common pets

explanation.surface: Pets backing away must keep something perfectly still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must keep' makes CITATS, and 'Retreating' turns the whole of it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not moving or changing is stationary, still.

clue.text: WWII veteran's language curbed by court

indicators.note: the court hems in the language

parts.note: Hindi is a major language of India

explanation.surface: An old soldier's language is restricted by a court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chindits were British-led special forces who fought behind Japanese lines in Burma in WWII.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Burma guerrilla brigade of the Second World War, now an old soldier.

clue.text: Guts shown by couple turning and smothering last of fire

parts.note: a duo is a couple, a pair

indicators.note: the reversed word covers the letter, as a blanket smothers a fire
the word and is turned to read backwards
the final letter of fire is wanted

explanation.surface: A couple turn round and smother a fire, showing their guts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes DNA from AND, and 'smothering' puts E (last of fire) inside to give DENA.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the first sections of the small intestine, plural, so guts in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Face punched by officer, rising skilfully

indicators.note: the officer punches a hole in the facing word

parts.note: to face down danger is to defy it

indicators.note: in a down answer rising reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: LT is lieutenant

explanation.surface: An officer punches someone in the face, rising up with skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' applies only to the officer, read upwards before 'punched by' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Done with neat dexterity, nimbly and adroitly.

clue.text: Performer playing sitar with extremely trite accompaniment

indicators.note: playing the letters treats them loosely, rearranging them
takes the extreme letters, first and last, of trite

explanation.surface: A performer plays the sitar to a hackneyed backing track.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer, from the French word.

clue.text: Superstar on boundary

parts.note: in cricket, the on side is also called the leg side
an end is a limit, a boundary

explanation.surface: A star player hits one onto the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side (the batter's leg side) is also called leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A person so famous they are spoken of as a living myth.

clue.text: Singer with no regrets, if paid the rent?

indicators.note: rent here is the past tense of rend, so the words are torn apart and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone would have no regrets if only the rent were paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like the landlord's money but means torn apart. The singer's famous song is 'Non, je ne regrette rien'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French chanteuse whose signature song declares she regrets nothing.

clue.text: Pack lunch or deliver sandwiches

indicators.note: the word is held in the middle of the phrase, as filling in a sandwich

explanation.surface: Pack a lunch or have it delivered, the sandwiches anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack of animals or people is a large crowd, a mob.

clue.text: Spectacle's modest, 50 having withdrawn

indicators.note: the fifty has been taken out of the word for modest

parts.note: slight means modest, small in degree
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A show is modest after fifty performers pull out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight is something worth seeing, a spectacle or display.

clue.text: Waterfowl, say, including small ducks on the rise

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means reading from the bottom up
the example abbreviation holds the other letters

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by say
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the round shape of O

explanation.surface: Waterfowl, for example small ducks, take flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' makes ESOOG, and 'on the rise' turns it upwards. Ducks are noughts in cricket, so O shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A large water bird, a kind of web-footed fowl related to swans and ducks.

clue.text: Swimmer using river always stopped by lake

indicators.note: the lake plugs a gap within the word for always

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
L is an abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A swimmer always uses the river, though a lake gets in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eel, which migrates from the sea up rivers, so a fish that swims in them.

clue.text: Among clues I do dreadfully, one is to be savoured

indicators.note: the numeral sits among the rearranged letters
done dreadfully, the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A solver confesses that among clues they handle badly, one is still a pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' rearranges CLUES I DO, and 'Among' places I (one) within that anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or an experience worth savouring is tasty, a delight to the palate.

clue.text: Most dirty knees regularly scrubbed in spring

indicators.note: the picked letters go inside the word for spring

parts.note: to dart is to spring forward suddenly

indicators.note: every other letter is scrubbed out, keeping the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Filthy knees get a regular scrub in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly scrubbed' keeps K, E and S from knees, and 'in' puts them inside DART.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirtiest in the sense of most sinister or black, superlatives of a grimy, gloomy shade.

clue.text: Rob's cut and run before church

indicators.note: the running comes first, ahead of the church

parts.note: to cut and run is to flee
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A man named Rob has cut and run before church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' looks like a man's name but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle someone out of money, overcharge them, is to strip them like shearing a sheep.
